description: Each service's own numbers, one tab per service. Counts read from a database work over any time range; panels read from traces cover the last 24 hours.

spec.title: Sign-in dialog
spec.description: Each hour's submissions of the sign-in dialog, by status: signing in, joining the waitlist and asking for a password reset. 303 signed a visitor in, and 200 recorded a waitlist request or sent a reset email. 400 refused an invalid form, 401 wrong credentials, 409 an email already on the waitlist or registered, 429 a visitor over the rate limit. Worry at any 5xx: Authentication could not answer.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "platform-account" && kind = server && name = "POST /(app)/(home)" } | count_over_time() by (span.http.response.status_code)

spec.title: Waitlist
spec.description: Each hour's waitlist requests, by Authentication's answer: 200 recorded the email, 409 found it already listed or registered, 429 refused a visitor over the rate limit. An invitation is the only way to an account, so worry at any 5xx: the request was lost, and the visitor saw an error.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "platform-account" && kind = client && span.http.request.method = "PUT" && span.url.path = "/v2/waitlist" } | count_over_time() by (span.http.response.status_code)

spec.title: Account changes
spec.description: Each hour's forms outside the sign-in dialog, by form and status. The account page changes a password, an email, the username or the picture, and signs out; the email links create an invited account, confirm an email or reset a password. 200 and 303 completed the step. 400 refused an invalid form, 403 a wrong current password. A link also answers 303 once it has expired, and 503 when the visitor hit the rate limit: Refusals from the services tells them apart. Worry at any other 5xx.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "platform-account" && kind = server && name =~ "POST .*" && name != "POST /(app)/(home)" } | count_over_time() by (name, span.http.response.status_code)

spec.title: Authorizations
spec.description: Each hour's authorization requests, through which an Agora app such as Studio signs its visitors in. 303 sent the visitor on: to the sign-in dialog, or back to the app with a code or an error. 400 refused a request naming no valid client to return to. Worry at any 5xx, or when 400s follow an app's release.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "platform-account" && kind = server && name = "GET /(app)/authorize" } | count_over_time() by (span.http.response.status_code)

spec.title: Calls to the services: p95
spec.description: How long the platform's server waits on each endpoint of Authentication, JSON Keys and Profile, at the 95th percentile. Every page a visitor with a session opens waits on GET /v2/session and GET /v1/profile/self, so worry when either climbs.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "platform-account" && kind = client && span.server.address =~ "rest[.](authentication|json-keys|profile)[.]svc" } | quantile_over_time(duration, .95) by (span.http.request.method, span.url.path)

spec.title: Refusals from the services
spec.description: Each hour's calls Authentication, JSON Keys or Profile answered with an error status, by endpoint and status: where a visitor's request met a limit, an expired link, a refused picture or a fault. A 404 on GET /v1/profile/self only means the visitor has no profile yet. Worry at any 5xx.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "platform-account" && kind = client && span.server.address =~ "rest[.](authentication|json-keys|profile)[.]svc" && span.http.response.status_code >= 400 } | count_over_time() by (span.http.request.method, span.url.path, span.http.response.status_code)

spec.title: Accounts
spec.description: Accounts by role, counted in the database.

spec.title: New accounts, 7 days
spec.description: Accounts created in the last 7 days, all roles.

spec.title: Codes mailed, 7 days
spec.description: What became of the codes mailed for a registration, an email change or a password reset. Used against mailed is the invitation or reset completion rate.

spec.title: Sign-ins by response
spec.description: Each hour's sign-in attempts by HTTP status: 200 signed in, 401 refused credentials, 429 rate-limited.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-authentication" && name = "rest.TokenCreate" } << { kind = server } | count_over_time() by (span.http.response.status_code)

spec.title: Mails sent
spec.description: Each hour's sends, by kind and status. A mail is sent once, never retried.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-authentication" && name = "core.MailDelivery(send)" } | count_over_time() by (span.mail.kind, status)

spec.title: Mails waiting or refused
spec.description: Mails that waited for a free sender, and mails refused because every sender was busy.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-authentication" && (name = "core.MailDelivery(wait)" || (name = "core.MailDelivery(reserve)" && status = error)) } | count_over_time() by (name)

spec.title: Refused refresh tokens
spec.description: Refreshes with a revoked or unknown token. A steady stream can mean a stolen token being replayed.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-authentication" && name = "core.TokenRefresh" && status = error && statusMessage =~ "refresh token (revoked|not issued).*" } | count_over_time()

spec.title: Authorization codes issued
spec.description: Each hour's sign-ins the account platform completed for another platform, by client. A client exchanges each code within minutes, so Authorization codes exchanged follows this count.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-authentication" && name = "core.AuthorizationCodeCreate" && status != error } | count_over_time() by (span.client.id)

spec.title: Authorization codes exchanged
spec.description: Each hour's codes a client traded for its tokens. Fewer exchanges than issued codes means people sign in but never reach the client: check its callback.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-authentication" && name = "core.TokenGrant" && span.oauth.grant_type = "authorization_code" && status != error } | count_over_time() by (span.client.id)

spec.title: Refused client token requests
spec.description: Each hour's refused code exchanges and refreshes, by client and OAuth error. Ended sessions refuse a few refreshes with invalid_grant. A burst can mean replayed codes or stolen refresh tokens, and invalid_client alone a caller outside the registry.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-authentication" && name = "core.TokenGrant" && span.oauth.error != nil } | count_over_time() by (span.client.id, span.oauth.error)

spec.title: Counter store
spec.description: Whether Valkey answers, how long since it started, and the memory its counters use against its cap. While it is down, each pod counts its rate limits on its own, and a restart empties the counters. Past 80% of the cap, raise it before Valkey evicts counters.

spec.title: Counters evicted
spec.description: Counters Valkey dropped each hour to stay under its memory cap. Each one loosens its limit until its window ends. It should stay at 0: an eviction alerts, and calls for a larger cap.

spec.title: Store commands
spec.description: The commands Valkey runs for the limiter each second, by command, and the average time it spends on one, on the right axis. Each limited request sends MGET, then INCRBY and EXPIRE inside MULTI and EXEC. PING runs only while a limit counts in its pod. A limit stops waiting on the store past 100 ms, so an average that climbs toward a millisecond means the store struggles.

spec.title: Counted in the pod
spec.description: The share of each rate-limited route's requests whose limits counted in the pod rather than in the store. A limit does so while the store fails or takes over 100 ms, until it answers again. It reads 0 on every route while the store counts them all. Above 0 for 5 minutes while the store is up, an alert fires: the pods cannot reach the store or log in.

spec.expr: sum by (span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="service-authentication", rate_limit_local="true"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (span_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="service-authentication"}[$__rate_interval])) or on () label_replace(vector(0), "span_name", "every route", "", "")

spec.title: Refused requests
spec.description: Each hour's requests refused with 429, by route: by a rate limit, or by a cap on the requests a route serves at once. The router's own limit refuses before any route matches, so its refusals read as the method alone. A steady stream on the sign-in routes can be password guessing; refusals on every route at once, limits too tight for real traffic.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-authentication" && kind = server && span.http.response.status_code = 429 } | count_over_time() by (name)

spec.title: Live generations
spec.description: Generations waiting for a provider call, and those a provider works on.

spec.title: Oldest waits
spec.description: The oldest waiting generation and the oldest running call. The sweep settles a call still running after two hours, so a running call older than that means the sweep stopped.

spec.title: Settled in the last hour
spec.description: Generations that reached a final status in the last hour, by reason, with the time from submission to settlement.

spec.title: Tokens, last 24 hours
spec.description: Tokens by model, reasoning effort and service tier: what the provider bills.

spec.title: Tokens per hour
spec.description: Input and output tokens the provider billed each hour.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-genai" && name = "dao.PgGenerationUsageInsert" } | sum_over_time(span.usage.input_tokens)
{ resource.service.name = "service-genai" && name = "dao.PgGenerationUsageInsert" } | sum_over_time(span.usage.output_tokens) by (name)

spec.title: Accounts generating, 24 hours
spec.description: Accounts that ran at least one generation in the last 24 hours.

spec.title: Refusals and provider pushback
spec.description: Each hour's submissions refused by a usage cap, and starts the provider turned away.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-genai" && (name = "core.GenerationCheck(failStart)" || (name = "core.GenerationSubmit(admit)" && status = error)) } | count_over_time() by (name)

spec.title: Provider calls: p95
spec.description: How long the calls to the model providers take, at the 95th percentile.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-genai" && kind = client && span.server.address != nil } | quantile_over_time(duration, .95) by (span.server.address)

spec.title: Kept past retention
spec.description: Settled generations still stored after their retention, which the purge deletes every 10 seconds. An alert fires past 30 minutes.

spec.title: Signing keys
spec.description: Each usage's active keys, the age of the newest, and the runway: how long the newest still signs. Rotation keeps the newest younger than its period; an alert fires when the runway drops under 3 days.

spec.title: Tokens signed
spec.description: Each hour's signed tokens by key usage: access tokens (auth) and refresh tokens (auth-refresh), which follow sign-ins.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-json-keys" && name = "core.ClaimsSign" } | count_over_time() by (span.key.usage)

spec.title: Key rotation runs
spec.description: The hourly rotation job's runs, by outcome.

spec.title: Token verifications refused
spec.description: Tokens Authentication refused to verify, each hour, by key usage: mostly expired tokens, so watch the trend.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-authentication" && name = "tokens.ClaimsVerify" && status = error } | count_over_time() by (span.key.usage)

spec.title: Public key reads
spec.description: Each hour's requests to the public REST API, by route and status: each platform pod reads the keys when its 30-minute cache expires, and the health check every 5 minutes. Worry at any 5xx, which keeps a platform from refreshing its keys.

spec.title: Sign-ins
spec.description: Each hour's sign-ins through the account platform, by step and status. sign-in sends the visitor there and callback brings them back, both with a 303; failed counts the returns that did not complete. Worry when failed follows callback, or at any 5xx.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "platform-studio" && (name = "GET /auth/sign-in" || name = "GET /auth/callback" || name = "GET /(studio)/auth/sign-in/failed") } | count_over_time() by (name, span.http.response.status_code)

spec.title: Pages and data requests
spec.description: Each hour's server renders: full pages, and data requests from pages already open.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "platform-studio" && kind = server } | count_over_time() by (span.sveltekit.is_data_request)

spec.title: Calls to the services: p95
spec.description: How long Studio's server waits on each service it calls, at the 95th percentile.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "platform-studio" && kind = client } | quantile_over_time(duration, .95) by (span.server.address)

spec.title: Refusals from the services
spec.description: Each hour's calls a service answered with an error status, by service and status: where a visitor's request met a limit or a fault. Profile answers 404 for a visitor who has no profile yet, so its 404s alone are no worry.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "platform-studio" && kind = client && span.http.response.status_code >= 400 } | count_over_time() by (span.server.address, span.http.response.status_code)

spec.title: Projects
spec.description: Every project the Scenes Composer stores, and those created in the last 7 days.

spec.title: Largest project
spec.description: The bytes the largest project stores, its own and those of everything in it, against the 16 MiB a project holds at most. A project at its cap refuses every write that grows it. Orange from 80%.

spec.title: Composer writes
spec.description: Each hour's writes to projects, scenes, beats, layers, cells and recaps, by route. Generations have their own panel.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-narrative-engine" && kind = server && name =~ "(POST|PUT|DELETE) /v1/.*" && name != "POST /v1/generation" && name != "DELETE /v1/generation" } | count_over_time() by (name)

spec.title: Project reads
spec.description: Each hour's reads of a whole project: loads, streams and manuscript exports. Each takes up to 128 MiB, and past one at a time per pod the others wait for a slot, so a burst here explains slow reads on Performance.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-narrative-engine" && kind = server && (name = "GET /v1/project" || name = "GET /v1/project/stream" || name = "GET /v1/manuscript") } | count_over_time() by (name)

spec.title: Generations
spec.description: Each hour's generation submits, cancels, and streams opened on a generation's calls.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-narrative-engine" && kind = server && (name = "POST /v1/generation" || name = "DELETE /v1/generation" || name = "GET /v1/generation/stream") } | count_over_time() by (name)

spec.title: Calls to GenAI
spec.description: Each hour's calls to GenAI, by method and gRPC status. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED is a user's usage cap, UNAVAILABLE an unreachable GenAI. Worry at UNAVAILABLE or INTERNAL that lasts.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-narrative-engine" && kind = client && name =~ "anovel[.]genai[.]v0[.].*" } | count_over_time() by (name, span.rpc.response.status_code)

spec.title: Refusals
spec.description: Each hour's requests answered with an error status, by route and status. 429 is a user's generation rate or the streams a caller holds open, 413 a body past its cap, 503 an unreachable GenAI or a planned downtime. Worry at any 500.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-narrative-engine" && kind = server && span.http.response.status_code >= 400 } | count_over_time() by (name, span.http.response.status_code)

spec.title: Profiles
spec.description: Every profile the service stores, those with a username and those with a picture, and the profiles created in the last 7 days. A picture weighs about 40 KB in the database: when pictures climb fast, check the profile database's volume on Health.

spec.title: Writes
spec.description: Each hour's username and picture writes, by route. Only the account page writes profiles, so a burst with no matching visitors on the account tab means a client repeats its writes.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-profile" && kind = server && (name = "PUT /v1/profile" || name = "PUT /v1/profile/picture" || name = "DELETE /v1/profile/picture") } | count_over_time() by (name)

spec.title: Refusals
spec.description: Each hour's refused writes: pictures by the rule they broke (format, ratio or dimensions), bodies over the 256 KiB cap, and 400 answers to a username update, which a refused username or a malformed body causes. The account page checks the same rules before it sends, so worry when refusals climb: a client skips the checks, or its rules and the service's differ.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-profile" && name = "core.decodePicture" && status = error } | count_over_time() by (span.error.type)
{ resource.service.name = "service-profile" && kind = server && span.http.response.status_code = 413 } | count_over_time() by (span.http.response.status_code)
{ resource.service.name = "service-profile" && kind = server && name = "PUT /v1/profile" && span.http.response.status_code = 400 } | count_over_time() by (name)

spec.title: Reads
spec.description: Each hour's profile and picture reads, by route. Browsers keep each picture version for a year, so picture reads follow new pictures and new visitors: a climb without either means browsers stopped caching them.

spec.query: { resource.service.name = "service-profile" && kind = server && (name = "GET /v1/profile" || name = "GET /v1/profile/self" || name = "GET /v1/profile/picture") } | count_over_time() by (name)
